finding.title: privacy-policy.md falsely claims no analytics/crash-report collection while release builds ship FirebaseAnalyticsService + unconditional Crashlytics
finding.why: The App Store/Play Store-facing privacy policy tells a parent installing this children's app that it does not collect 'Analytics events or usage telemetry' or 'Crash reports.' In reality, release/profile builds wire analyticsServiceProvider to a real FirebaseAnalyticsService (analytics_provider.dart:22-29) that sends named events with a content identifier (sefaria_ref) and per-child identifiers (profile_id, at analytics_service.dart:56,82,87 — already a baselined PV-1 code gap), and firebase_bootstrap.dart unconditionally enables Crashlytics collection and forwards the numeric profileId as the Crashlytics user identifier. This is not merely stale prose — it is a live, false representation to end users (and, given the app's stated child userbase, a child-privacy-adjacent misrepresentation) about what data leaves the device. Anyone who reads and relies on this policy — including a parent deciding whether to let a child use the app — is being told something the shipped binary does not do.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the 'Data We Do NOT Collect' section to remove the false 'Analytics events'/'Crash reports' bullets, add Firebase Analytics and Firebase Crashlytics to the 'Third-Party Services' table with their actual purpose (event/crash telemetry) and a link to Google's privacy policy, and state what parameters are sent. This is independent of (and does not replace) actually fixing the underlying PV-1/PV-3 code gaps (consent-gating, dropping content/profile identifiers from event params) already tracked in coding-standards.md — but until those land, the policy must describe reality, not the target state.
acceptance_criteria: privacy-policy.md's collection list and third-party table match what analyticsServiceProvider/FirebaseCrashlyticsService actually send in a release build
a lightweight CI/doc-review check (or a checklist item in the PV-1/PV-3 remediation ticket) requires updating this doc in the same PR that changes analytics/crashlytics consent behavior
